name: Gmail
description: Read, send, search, label, draft, and archive Gmail. 36 tools across messages, threads, labels, drafts, and filters. Bundled local stdio MCP — no npx download required, ships with the Vodou install.

setupSteps.title: Create Google Cloud OAuth credentials
setupSteps.instructions: Open console.cloud.google.com → APIs & Services → Credentials. Click Create credentials → OAuth client ID. Pick Desktop app as the application type. Name it Vodou Gmail. Click Create, then Download JSON.
setupSteps.gotcha: Make sure the Gmail API is enabled at APIs & Services → Library → Gmail API → Enable.

setupSteps.title: Save credentials.json into the gmail folder
setupSteps.instructions: Move the downloaded JSON to MCP-servers/gmail/credentials.json inside your Vodou install directory. The launcher reads this file to know which OAuth client to use.
setupSteps.gotcha: The file MUST be named credentials.json exactly. The launcher won't find it under any other name.

setupSteps.title: Run the one-time auth flow
setupSteps.instructions:
In a terminal, from your Vodou install root, run:
node MCP-servers/gmail/auth.js
Your browser opens a Google consent screen. Click Allow for read/send/modify/labels scopes. Tokens get cached to MCP-servers/gmail/tokens.json and auto-refresh from then on.
setupSteps.gotcha: If your browser doesn't open automatically, copy the URL printed in the terminal and paste it manually.

setupSteps.title: Add server
setupSteps.instructions: Click Add server below. Vodou runs vodou-core connect gmail which spawns the bundled launcher with your cached tokens. The launcher refreshes the access token automatically on each spawn.
setupSteps.gotcha: If you see a No tokens found error after Add server, you skipped the auth step above — re-run node MCP-servers/gmail/auth.js first.

setupSteps.title: Enable in Tools
setupSteps.instructions: Open Capabilities → MCP Servers and turn gmail on. You'll get 36 tools: messages_list, message_get, message_send, message_search, thread_get, label_create, draft_create, etc. Try saying 'check my inbox' or 'send an email to ...' in chat.
